profiler.name: NVIDIA Nsight Compute Command Line Profiler
profiler.root: sudo on the board, with the account password on stdin; `perf_event_paranoid=2` and no NOPASSWD

board.name: Pinkie
board.clock: 2026-09-02T14:30Z (the board runs ~9 days behind the dev host, D-010)
board.shared: llama-server (pid 1304, --n-gpu-layers 99) has been resident since board clock 2026-09-01T16:56, so the GPU was not exclusively held

source.transfer: git archive HEAD | gzip, scp to the board, untar under the account home
source.build: CUDAARCHS=87-real NVCC=/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc cargo test -p qualia-cuda --features cuda --release --test gpu --offline -j 2 --no-run
source.build_evidence: the build log records `qualia-cuda: embedded fatbins for sm_87`

environment.why: CUDA forward-compatibility libcuda; the board's toolkit 12.9 is newer than its driver 540.4, so without it cuModuleLoadData fails with CUDA_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_PTX_VERSION (D-016, T50)

capture_range_note: --launch-count 8, the suite's own launch count; the profiler keeps running past the eighth launch, so `smoke`'s `add_one` loop is not in the capture (the same cut T18 records)
measurement_note: one pass, ncu's default clock control; the board's SM Frequency read 305.98 MHz for these launches, and the durations are far below `docs/evidence/T18/fatbin-sm-87`'s 13.00 ms `belief_update` on the same board and 39.32 ms total. Reported as measured, with no claim attached to the difference
kernels_json: hand-normalised projection of metrics.csv, one object per launch; see the directory README for the column mapping and the export's hashes
no_display_devices_touched: no adapter was disabled, enabled or restarted, and no driver was reinstalled (D-012)
